hypothesis: TS #2483 (stale perf PR, not superseded): settled RLM children hold a worker and a kernel until parent close - nothing at the tip releases them (the supersession analysis measured ~141-244MB worker + ~30MB kernel per settled child). The TS inline arm (a snapshot-flushing stopKernel that keeps the child session live, listable, inspectable, collectable, and deletable, with the next kernel use reviving from the flushed snapshot) ports to the rust worker architecture as: (1) IpythonKernelProvisioner::stop_kernel (the revivable snapshot-flushing stop + the pendingStop revival gate), and (2) the worker-side settle-conditioned release (the child worker's own turn-runner park arm fires it when the parent-owned, unattached, unqueued idle state holds and the engine gates pass: no unsettled descendants, no registered cron/heartbeat jobs). The roster and collect surfaces are untouched by design (byte-identical); the daemon-mode whole-worker passivation stays DEFERRED to the orchestrator per the lane brief.
approach: PHASE 0 the supersession analysis (the predecessor's, accepted): #2483 not superseded; the inline arm in scope; the whole-worker passivation deferred. PHASE 1 the port (branch lane/perf-revive-2483 off the SETTLED tip 944017dd7, all three split series complete): IpythonKernelProvisioner::stop_kernel (TS stopKernel: snapshot + drain_host_requests shutdown without disposing; the in-flight-startup arm joins the boot then shuts the kernel down, the TS managerPromise arm; the pendingStop gate as a clonable watch receiver so multiple revival waiters gate on it - a completed stop awaits instantly, each stop supersedes), start_kernel_impl awaits the stop gate before reading the snapshot back; the session engine's stop_kernel_snapshot seam beside dispose_kernel; the SessionEngine trait's release_settled_child_kernel (default no-op for scripted harness engines) implemented by AgentSessionEngine with the canPassivateSettledSession gates engine-side (has_unsettled_rlm_work for descendants, a worker-wired registered-jobs probe over the shared cron store for hasRegisteredCronJob) firing the per-build weak-provisioner release probe (the background-bash-probe adoption pattern, cleared on retire/close); the turn runner's park arm fires it best-effort when the worker core proves parent-owned (rlm_depth>0) + unattached + not compacting + no lane work (the park arm's construction). PHASE 2 gates: lane VM cargo fmt --all --check rc=0, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings rc=0 (four authoring iterations: a lost struct-field edit, tokio JoinHandle-not-Clone -> the watch receiver, a single_match_else, a Send-guard-across-await), the three test pieces green. PHASE 3 fleet review + full-suite gate on the org head 97b38836d. PHASE 4 the daemon-mode settled-child census (same-VM sequential A/B, the mock-provider-scripted spawn through the parent's kernel rlm.spawn, ppid-attributed process-tree census at settle). PHASE 5 fleet review x2 + gate x2 on the pre-fix and folded heads with every red triaged solo-green on the exact head content.
parity_notes: FROZEN SURFACES: no wire or schema change (no new DaemonCommand; the frozen roster/collect paths untouched by design - the release touches only the kernel lifecycle); the session-JSONL/TUI/prompt surfaces untouched. THE DISCLOSED INTERNAL DIVERGENCE: the TS release is parent-driven at the parent's run-settle hook (TS children are in-process sessions, so the parent reaches the child's provisioner directly); the rust children are WORKER PROCESSES (the parent has no in-process reach and the daemon wire is a frozen surface), so the port triggers the release at the child's OWN idle park arm - the same revivability semantics (the next kernel use boots fresh from the flushed snapshot through the pendingStop gate), the same policy gates (parent-owned, unattached, idle, no descendants busy, no registered cron jobs), and the same best-effort failure class (a failed stop leaves the kernel resident; the child stays listable/inspectable/collectable/deletable). The per-turn granularity note: the TS releases once per settled run; the park arm fires at every idle park (a stop with no live kernel is a no-op, and a follow-up prompt's first kernel use revives from the snapshot - the TS's own accepted revival cost class).
